Calculate Forward Rates from DNS Factors

Source: R/dns-simulation.r
calculate_dns_forwards.Rd

Calculates instantaneous forward rates based on DNS factors.

Usage

calculate_dns_forwards(factors, maturities, lambda = ns_lambda(3.5))

Arguments

factors

Matrix or array. DNS factors.

maturities

Numeric vector. Maturities (in years) for forward rates.

lambda

Numeric. DNS decay parameter lambda, per unit of maturity. Maturities here are in years, and the default places the curvature hump at 3.5 years, near the middle of a Treasury curve. It is written as ns_lambda(3.5) so the number states its own meaning; see ns_lambda. Diebold and Li's 0.0609 is a month-denominated constant and in years would place that hump at 29.4 years.

Value

Matrix or array of forward rates with the same structure as the yield output from calculate_dns_yields.

Details

The instantaneous forward rate in the DNS model is given by: $$f(m) = \beta_1 + \beta_2 e^{-\lambda m} + \beta_3 \lambda m e^{-\lambda m}$$

Examples

maturities <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 30)
factors <- matrix(c(0.035, -0.015, 0.005), nrow = 1)

# Forwards sit above spots where the curve is rising
rbind(
  spot = calculate_dns_yields(factors, maturities, ns_lambda(3.5))[1, ],
  forward = calculate_dns_forwards(factors, maturities, ns_lambda(3.5))[1, ]
)
#>               [,1]       [,2]       [,3]       [,4]       [,5]       [,6]
#> spot    0.02121510 0.02230819 0.02417968 0.02694920 0.02881798 0.03101193
#> forward 0.02236687 0.02438143 0.02754859 0.03145546 0.03342735 0.03483095
#>               [,7]       [,8]       [,9]      [,10]
#> spot    0.03215056 0.03303012 0.03402399 0.03434942
#> forward 0.03508122 0.03506322 0.03500128 0.03500001
